_comment: Co-purchase bundles. Curated from Houzz 2024-2025 trends (84-87% of vanity replacements include faucet; 87% of shower remodels replace wall tile; etc.), Lowe's allen+roth collections, Home Depot Glacier Bay, IKEA named series, NKBA bathroom zone conventions. Each bundle is what real shoppers buy together in a single project — not a guess. The agent retrieves bundles by anchor category + scope and proposes them as coordinated sets via proposeProductGrid.

bundles.name: Vanity Wall Refresh
bundles.frequency_data: 84-87% of vanity replacements include the faucet (Houzz 2024). Mirror + light upgrade rate together ~62%.
bundles.designer_voice: The vanity is the anchor — mirror, faucet, and light all live in its finish family. Get those four right and the wall reads as designed, not assembled.

bundles.name: Shower Zone Refresh
bundles.frequency_data: 87% of shower remodels replace wall tile, 83% floor tile, 84% showerhead (Houzz 2024). Joint floor ≥71%.
bundles.designer_voice: Wet zone is one decision: the showerhead/valve pair sets the finish, the wall tile sets the palette, the floor tile carries through. Anything mismatched here shows up first.

bundles.name: Tub Zone Refresh
bundles.frequency_data: Tub replacements average 4-piece bundle; freestanding tubs imply deck-mount or floor-mount filler (different forms).
bundles.designer_voice: Tub style locks the filler form. Freestanding = floor-mount filler statement piece; alcove = deck-mount minimal. Drain finish matches the filler.

bundles.name: Hardware Refresh
bundles.frequency_data: Finish-only refresh ($300-800) — popular for $5K-under partial projects. Pottery Barn Mercer / RH Lugarno pattern.
bundles.designer_voice: Cheapest way to change the feel of a bathroom. Lock one finish across every piece of metal you touch — that's the only rule.

bundles.name: Powder Room Starter
bundles.designer_voice: Powder room = the bathroom guests see. Spend the personality budget here — bold finish, statement vanity. Five pieces, all coordinated.

bundles.name: Three-Quarter Bath Starter
bundles.designer_voice: Three-quarter bath = the working bathroom. Function leads — pick durable finishes, easy-clean tile. One bold metal, one accent.

bundles.name: Primary Bath Starter
bundles.designer_voice: Primary bath = your space, your rules. Two finishes work here — typically one cool + one warm metal — as long as they show up in pairs (not orphaned). Tub and walk-in shower as separate destinations.

bundles.name: Toilet + Safety Accessories
bundles.designer_voice: Aging-in-place starts with the toilet. Comfort-height seat, grab bar in reach, finish that doesn't shout 'medical'. Brushed nickel reads warmer than chrome here.

bundles.name: Mirror + Light Pair
bundles.designer_voice: Mirror frame and the vanity light over it are the most-seen pair in any bathroom. Same finish, scaled — light bar should be 60-75% of vanity width.

bundles.name: Spa Wellness Add-On
bundles.designer_voice: Spa is a temperature. Warm metals (brass, bronze, aged), warm light (≤2700K, dimmable), warm textures (towel warmer ready, stone). Polished cool finishes break it.
